IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p122/r1.anchor: فلياتكم برزق منه أي بما تأكلونه وليتلطف أي ليدقق النظر فيه

SAMIN-DURR:18:19/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:19/r1.speaker: الزجاج والزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:18:19/r1.claim: كذلك means “as we put them to sleep, so we awakened them”; that refers to the sleeping act, making awakening another sign.
SAMIN-DURR:18:19/r1.anchor: الكاف نعت لمصدر محذوف، أي: كما أنمناهم

SAMIN-DURR:18:19/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:19/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:18:19/r2.claim: Ibn Atiyya takes ليتساءلوا as eventual result because awakening was not intended for questioning; the author prefers causal purpose.
SAMIN-DURR:18:19/r2.anchor: الكاف نعت لمصدر محذوف، أي: كما أنمناهم

SAMIN-DURR:18:19/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:19/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:19/r3.claim: كم is adverbial with “days” omitted, supplied by the answer.
SAMIN-DURR:18:19/r3.anchor: الكاف نعت لمصدر محذوف، أي: كما أنمناهم

SAMIN-DURR:18:19/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:19/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:19/r4.claim: أو in أو بعض يوم may express uncertainty or distribute the answers among different speakers.
SAMIN-DURR:18:19/r4.anchor: الكاف نعت لمصدر محذوف، أي: كما أنمناهم

SAMIN-DURR:18:19/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:19/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:19/r5.claim: بورقكم is circumstantial to أحدكم, meaning he goes accompanied by or carrying it.
SAMIN-DURR:18:19/r5.anchor: الكاف نعت لمصدر محذوف، أي: كما أنمناهم

SAMIN-DURR:18:19/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:19/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:19/r6.claim: Abu Amr, Hamza, and Abu Bakr use fatḥa waw with silent ra; the others use the original kasra, while sukun is easing.
SAMIN-DURR:18:19/r6.anchor: الكاف نعت لمصدر محذوف، أي: كما أنمناهم

SAMIN-DURR:18:19/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:19/r7.speaker: الزجاج
SAMIN-DURR:18:19/r7.claim: Al-Zajjaj transmits kasra waw with silent ra, comparing vowel variants like كبد.
SAMIN-DURR:18:19/r7.anchor: الكاف نعت لمصدر محذوف، أي: كما أنمناهم

SAMIN-DURR:18:19/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:19/r8.speaker: أبو رجاء وابن محيصن
SAMIN-DURR:18:19/r8.claim: They also read it this way but assimilate قاف; critics object to two adjoining sukun letters. Ibn Muhaysin is also reported to assimilate ra's kasra.
SAMIN-DURR:18:19/r8.anchor: الكاف نعت لمصدر محذوف، أي: كما أنمناهم

SAMIN-DURR:18:19/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:19/r9.speaker: أمير المؤمنين
SAMIN-DURR:18:19/r9.claim: A reading بوارقكم means “the possessor of silver”; ورق may also be a collective noun.
SAMIN-DURR:18:19/r9.anchor: الكاف نعت لمصدر محذوف، أي: كما أنمناهم

SAMIN-DURR:18:19/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:19/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:19/r10.claim: ورق means coined silver or silver generally; الرقة omits its first فاء; hadith says it owes one quarter of a tenth.
SAMIN-DURR:18:19/r10.anchor: الكاف نعت لمصدر محذوف، أي: كما أنمناهم

SAMIN-DURR:18:19/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:19/r11.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:19/r11.claim: أي in أيها أزكى may be interrogative or relative; أهلها is understood and طعاما is a tamyiz.
SAMIN-DURR:18:19/r11.anchor: الكاف نعت لمصدر محذوف، أي: كما أنمناهم

SAMIN-DURR:18:19/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:19/r12.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:19/r12.claim: Alternatively there is no ellipsis: its pronoun refers to foods understood in context.
SAMIN-DURR:18:19/r12.anchor: الكاف نعت لمصدر محذوف، أي: كما أنمناهم

SAMIN-DURR:18:19#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:19#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:19#2/r1.claim: Most readers use sukun on command-lām in وليتلطف; al-Hasan uses the original kasra.
SAMIN-DURR:18:19#2/r1.anchor: قرأ العامة بسكون لام الأمر، والحسن بكسرها على الأصل

SAMIN-DURR:18:19#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:19#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:19#2/r2.claim: Qutayba al-Mayyāl reads وليتلطف in the passive.
SAMIN-DURR:18:19#2/r2.anchor: قرأ العامة بسكون لام الأمر، والحسن بكسرها على الأصل

SAMIN-DURR:18:19#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:19#2/r3.speaker: أبو جعفر وأبو صالح وقتيبة
SAMIN-DURR:18:19#2/r3.claim: They read ولا يشعرن with open ياء and damma عين; أحد is the subject.
SAMIN-DURR:18:19#2/r3.anchor: قرأ العامة بسكون لام الأمر، والحسن بكسرها على الأصل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p145/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p145/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p145/r1.claim: After 309 years, God raised the youths with their bodies, hair, and skin unchanged.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p145/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p145/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p145/r2.claim: They guessed they had slept a day or part of one because they entered early in the day and awoke late, then admitted God knew best how long it was.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p145/r2.anchor: كان دخولهم إلى الكهف في أول نهار

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p145/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p145/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p145/r3.claim: They turned to their more urgent need for food and drink and sent one of their number with their silver coins to the city from which they had departed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p145/r3.anchor: ثم عدلوا إلى الأهم في أمرهم إذ ذاك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p145/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p145/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p145/r4.claim: They had brought coins from home for their needs and spent some, leaving the remaining silver to take to their city.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p145/r4.anchor: وذلك أنهم كانوا قد استصحبوا معهم دراهم من منازلهم لحاجتهم إليها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p145#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p145#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p145#2/r1.claim: Azka taaman most likely means tastiest or purest food, supported by 24:21 and 87:14 and the root sense of purifying; another view takes it as more abundant, as a poetic line suggests, but the youths sought lawful wholesome food regardless of quantity.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p145#2/r1.anchor: مقصودهم إنما هو الطيب الحلال، سواء كان قليلا أو كثيرا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p145#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p145#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p145#2/r2.claim: Let him be discreet in going, shopping, and returning; do not let anyone know about you.

JISHUMI:v6p4377#2/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4377#2/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو وحمزة وأبو بكر عن عاصم
JISHUMI:v6p4377#2/r1.claim: They read بورقكم with a still rāʾ; the other readers kasra it, and Abū ʿAmr also assimilates qāf into kāf. The variants retain the same meaning: silver, coined or uncoined.
JISHUMI:v6p4377#2/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو وحمزة وأبو بكر عن عاصم: بورقكم ساكنة الراء،

JISHUMI:v6p4377#2/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4377#2/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4377#2/r2.claim: Baʿth originally means stirring something up and also means sending messengers or raising the dead.
JISHUMI:v6p4377#2/r2.anchor: البعث: أصله الإثارة، ثم يستعمل في أشياء، يقال: بعث الله الأنبياء أرسلهم،

JISHUMI:v6p4377#2/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4377#2/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4377#2/r3.claim: Zakā can mean growth or purity, as in the verse about purifying them.
JISHUMI:v6p4377#2/r3.anchor: والزكاة: قيل: أصلها النماء، يقال: زكا الزرع، وقيل: أصلها الطهارة ومنه الزكاة،

JISHUMI:v6p4377#2/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4377#2/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4377#2/r4.claim: Luṭf can mean smallness, gentleness in an action, or God's kindness and mercy.
JISHUMI:v6p4377#2/r4.anchor: واللطف: صغر الشيء، واللطف في الأعمال: الرفق بها، واللطف من الله تعالى: الرأفة والرحمة،

JISHUMI:v6p4377#2/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4377#2/r6.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v6p4377#2/r6.claim: The likeness in ‘thus We raised them’ compares raising them from sleep to preserving them during their long sleep; either act exceeds anyone's power but God's.
JISHUMI:v6p4377#2/r6.anchor: كما حفظناهم في تلك المدة بعثناهم عن تلك الرقدة لنعرفهم عجيب أمرنا

JISHUMI:v6p4377#2/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4377#2/r7.speaker: الأصم
JISHUMI:v6p4377#2/r7.claim: He says they were raised in exactly the condition in which they had fallen asleep, with nothing changed.
JISHUMI:v6p4377#2/r7.anchor: على الحالة التي وقدوا عليها بعثناهم لم يتغير شيء من ذلك، عن الأصم.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r1.claim: Their awakening, like their sleep, displays God’s power over both sleep and resurrection, prompts inquiry, reflection and certainty, and calls for gratitude.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r1.anchor: وكما أنمناهم تلك النومة كذلك بعثناهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r2.claim: Their estimate of a day or part of one rests on predominant conjecture; this permits ijtihad and probable judgment, which may be mistaken without being a lie.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r2.anchor: جواب مبني على غالب الظن . وفيه دليل على جواز الاجتهاد والقول بالظن الغالب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r3.claim: Some correct the others: the duration was long, known only to God, perhaps inferred from evidence or divine inspiration.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r3.anchor: إنكار عليهم من بعضهم ، وأن الله أعلم بمدة لبثهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r4.speaker: رُوي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r4.claim: They entered the cave in the morning and awoke after noon, first supposing it was still the same day; their long nails and hair prompted their estimate.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r4.anchor: روي أنهم دخلوا الكهف غدوة وكان انتباههم بعد الزوال

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r5.claim: Their turn to sending someone for food means they stop debating an unknowable duration and attend to a more urgent need.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r5.anchor: لا طريق لكم إلى علمه ، فخذوا في شيء آخر مما يهمكم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r6.claim: Wariq means silver, whether minted or unminted.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r6.anchor: والورق : الفضة ، مضروبة كانت أو غير مضروبة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r7.claim: A report says ʿArfaja lost his nose at the battle of al-Kulab, tried a silver replacement that smelled, and was ordered to use gold.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r7.anchor: أن عرفجة أصيب أنفه يوم الكلاب فاتخذ أنفا من ورق فأنتن ، فأمره رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r8.claim: Wariq is read with the ra still or moving; Ibn Kathir has kasra on ra and assimilates qaf into kaf.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r8.anchor: وقرىء : ( بورقكم ) بسكون الراء والواو مفتوحة أو مكسورة . وقرأ ابن كثير ( بورقكم ) ، بكسر الراء وإدغام القاف في الكاف

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r9.speaker: ابن محيصن
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r9.claim: Ibn Muhaysin reads waw with kasra, ra still, and assimilation; al-Zamakhshari rejects it as an impermissible meeting of two still letters.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r9.anchor: وعن ابن محيصن أنه كسر الواو وأسكن الراء وأدغم ، وهذا غير جائز لالتقاء الساكنين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r11.claim: Their carrying travel provisions and money exemplifies the prudent reliance of those who trust God, rather than relying on chance or others’ stores.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r11.anchor: دليل على أن حمل النفقة وما يصلح المسافر هو رأي المتوكلين على الله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r12.speaker: عائشة رضي الله عنها
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r12.claim: Aisha told someone asking about a pilgrim in ihram fastening his money belt to secure his provisions.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r12.anchor: ومنه قول عائشة رضي الله عنها لمن سألها عن محرم يشد عليه هميانه : أوثق عليك نفقتك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r13.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r13.claim: He recounts an ascetic scholar who declined wealthy townspeople’s offers to finance pilgrimage, saying travel requires a money belt and trust in the Merciful.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r13.anchor: ما لهذا السفر إلا شيآن : شد الهميان ، والتوكل على الرحمن

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r14.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r14.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r14.claim: “Among them” means among the city’s people, with “people” elided as in the command to ask the town.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r14.anchor: بينهم } أي أهلها ، فحذف الأهل كما في قوله { واسئل القرية }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r15.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r15.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r15.claim: Azka food may mean most lawful, pleasant, abundant, or inexpensive.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r15.anchor: أزكى طعاما } أحل وأطيب وأكثر وأرخص

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r16.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r16.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r16.claim: “Be tactful” may mean taking care in the purchase to avoid being cheated, or keeping discreet so no one recognizes the envoy.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r16.anchor: وليتلطف } وليتكلف اللطف والنيقة فيما يباشره من أمر المبايعة حتى لا يغبن

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r17.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r17.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r17.claim: The warning not to let anyone know includes avoiding actions that unintentionally cause people to notice them; the wording calls that causing awareness.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r17.anchor: يعني : ولا يفعلن ما يؤدي من غير قصد منه إلى الشعور بنا ، فسمى ذلك إشعارا منه بهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r18.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r18.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r18.claim: The pronoun in “they” refers to the implied people of the city in “among them.”
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p663/r18.anchor: الضمير في { إنهم } راجع إلى الأهل المقدر في { بينهم }

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p293/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p293/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p293/r1.claim: Their being raised means that they were awakened; God also put their dog to sleep with them, according to Muqatil.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p293/r1.anchor: يعني به إيقاظهم من نومهم . قال مقاتل : وأنام الله كلبهم معهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p293/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p293/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p293/r2.claim: They asked each other how long they had slept so they could determine its duration.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p293/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p293/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p293/r3.claim: One youth guessed they had slept a day because that was the longest familiar sleep; seeing the sun still up, he revised it to part of a day, since they had slept early and awakened late.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p293/r3.anchor: كان السائل منهم أحدهم , والمجيب له غيره , فقال لبثنا يوما لأنه أطول مدة النوم المعهود , فلما رأى الشمس لم تغرب قال { أو بعض يوما } لأنهم أنيموا أول النهار ونبهوا آخره

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p293/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p293/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p293/r4.claim: ربكم أعلم بما لبثتم may be God's statement that He knows the length of their stay.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p293/r4.anchor: أنه حكاية عن الله تعالى أنه أعلم بمدة لبثهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p293/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p293/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p293/r5.claim: Alternatively, the eldest youth Maksalmina ended the disagreement by saying that their Lord knows how long they stayed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p293/r5.anchor: فنطق بالصواب ورد الأمر إلى الله عالمه , وهذا قول ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p293/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p293/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p293/r6.claim: The word ورق is read with either a kasra or a silent rāʾ, and in both readings means silver coins; ورق with a fatḥa means camels or sheep.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p293/r6.anchor: قرىء بكسر الراء وبتسكينها , وهو في القراءتين جميعا الدراهم , وأما الورق بفتح الراء فهي الإبل والغنم

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p293/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p293/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p293/r7.claim: A poem uses ورقي for a person's camels and sheep, supporting the livestock sense with fatḥa.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p293/r7.anchor:
إياك أدعو فتقبل ملقي … كفر خطاياي وثمر ورقي
يعني إبله وغنمه

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p293/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p293/r8.speaker: عكرمة
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p293/r8.claim: أزكى طعاما may mean the greatest quantity of food.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p293/r8.anchor: أيها أكثر طعاما , وهذا قول عكرمة

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p293/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p293/r9.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p293/r9.claim: أزكى طعاما may mean the most lawful food.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p293/r9.anchor: أيها أحل طعاما , وهذا قول قتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p293/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p293/r10.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p293/r10.claim: أزكى طعاما may mean the tastiest food.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p293/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p293/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p293/r11.claim: A further interpretation takes أزكى طعاما to mean the cheapest food.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p293/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p293/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p293/r12.claim: فليأتكم برزق منه may mean bringing food for them to eat.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p293/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p293/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p293/r13.claim: Alternatively, it means bringing food lawful for them to eat.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p293/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p293/r14.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p293/r14.claim: وليتلطف may mean bargaining carefully for a low price.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p293/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p293/r15.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p293/r15.claim: Alternatively, it means being discreet about their situation.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p293/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p293/r16.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p293/r16.claim: The instruction supports sharing food and pooled costs among a group, a practice called munāhada that pre-Islamic Arabs disapproved of but Islamic law permits.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p293/r16.anchor: وهذا يدل على جواز اشتراك الجماعة في طعامهم وإن كان بعضهم أكثر أكلا وهي المناهدة , وكانت مستقبحة في الجاهلية فجاء الشرع بإباحتها

MUQATIL:18:18-21/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:18-21/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:18-21/r6.claim: God awakens them to question one another; Maksalmina, the oldest, asks how long they have slept.
MUQATIL:18:18-21/r6.anchor: قال قائل منهم } ، وهومكسلمينا، وهو أكبرهم سنا، { كم لبثتم } رقودا، { قالوا لبثنا يوما } ،

MUQATIL:18:18-21/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:18-21/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:18-21/r7.claim: They guess one day or part of a day because they entered the cave in the morning and awoke near the day's end.
MUQATIL:18:18-21/r7.anchor: وكانوا دخلوا الغار غدوة، وبعثوا من آخر النهار، فمن ثم قالوا: { أو بعض يوم قالوا } ،

MUQATIL:18:18-21/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:18-21/r8.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:18-21/r8.claim: Maksalmina alone tells them their Lord knows their duration better, returning the matter to God.
MUQATIL:18:18-21/r8.anchor: قالوا } ، يعني الأكبر، وهو مكسلمينا وحده، { ربكم أعلم بما لبثتم } في رقودكم منكم،

MUQATIL:18:18-21/r9.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:18-21/r9.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:18-21/r9.claim: Maksalmina proposes sending one of them to town with their coins; they send Yamliha.
MUQATIL:18:18-21/r9.anchor: فابعثوا أحدكم بورقكم } ، يعني الدراهم، { هذه } التى معكم، { إلى المدينة } ، فبعثوا يمليخا،

MUQATIL:18:18-21/r10.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:18-21/r10.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:18-21/r10.claim: Azka food means the tastiest food; the messenger should act discreetly so no one notices or learns their whereabouts.
MUQATIL:18:18-21/r10.anchor: فلينظر أيهآ أزكى طعاما } ، يعني أطيب طعاما، { فليأتكم برزق منه وليتلطف } ، يعني وليترفق

NASAFI-FULL:v3p7/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p7/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p7/r1.claim: As God made them sleep, He awakened them too, displaying His power over both sleep and resurrection.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p7/r1.anchor: وكما أنمناهم تلك النومة كذلك أيقظناهم اظهارا للقدرة على الانامة والبعث

NASAFI-FULL:v3p7/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p7/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p7/r2.claim: Their questioning helps them learn what happened, reflect on God's power, increase certainty, and give thanks for His favor.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p7/r2.anchor: ليسأل بعضهم بعضا ويتعرفوا حالهم وما صنع الله بهم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p7/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p7/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p7/r3.claim: The questioner was their leader, who asked how long they had stayed.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p7/r3.anchor: ﴿ قال قائل منهم ﴾ رئيسهم ﴿ كم لبثتم ﴾

NASAFI-FULL:v3p7/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p7/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p7/r4.claim: Their answer of a day or part of one rests on predominant conjecture and shows that reasoning and acting on such conjecture are permissible.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p7/r4.anchor: جواب مبني على غالب الظن وفيه دليل على جواز الاجتهاد والقول بالظن الغالب

NASAFI-FULL:v3p7/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p7/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p7/r5.claim: Some answered that God knew best after signs or inspiration showed them the stay had been long and its exact duration was known only to Him.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p7/r5.anchor: انكار عليهم من بعضهم كأنهم قد علموا بالأدلة أو بالهام أن المدة متطاولة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p7/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p7/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p7/r6.claim: A report says they entered in the morning and woke after noon, then judged from their long nails and hair that the sleep had lasted a long time.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p7/r6.anchor: روى أنهم دخلوا الكهف غدوة وكان انتباههم بعد الزوال

NASAFI-FULL:v3p7/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p7/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
NASAFI-FULL:v3p7/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās inferred that the sleepers were seven from the singular questioner, the plural answer, and a further plural reply.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p7/r7.anchor: وقد استدل ابن عباس رضي الله عنه على أن الصحيح أن عددهم سبعة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p7/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p7/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p7/r8.claim: One of them was sent, namely Tamlīkha; wariq is silver, whether coined or uncoined, and several readers pronounce its rāʾ still.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p7/r8.anchor: كأنهم قالوا ربكم أعلم بذلك لا طريق لكم إلى علمه

NASAFI-FULL:v3p7/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p7/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p7/r9.claim: The city is Tarsus; taking provisions for travel is proper for those who trust God, unlike relying on chance or empty claims of reliance.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p7/r9.anchor: هي طرسوس وحملهم الورق عند فرارهم دليل على أن حمل النفقة وما يصلح للمسافر

NASAFI-FULL:v3p7/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p7/r10.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p7/r10.claim: Some scholars, longing for the Sacred House, said travel requires only packed provisions and trust in the Merciful.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p7/r10.anchor: وعن بعض العلماء أنه كان شديد الحنين إلى بيت الله ويقول ما لهذا السفر إلا

NASAFI-FULL:v3p7/r11.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p7/r11.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p7/r11.claim: In “which of them,” the أهلها is elided, as in “ask the town”; azkā can mean more lawful, wholesome, plentiful, or cheaper.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p7/r11.anchor: أي أهلها فحذف كما في واسئل القرية

NASAFI-FULL:v3p7/r12.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p7/r12.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p7/r12.claim: Ṭaʿāman is a specification (tamyīz), and the envoy should obtain provisions from the food he finds.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p7/r13.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p7/r13.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p7/r13.claim: He should act gently in the purchase so he is not cheated, or remain discreet so no one recognizes him.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p7/r13.anchor: وليتكلف اللطف فيما يباشره من أمر المبايعة حتى لا يغبن أو في أمر التخفي

NASAFI-FULL:v3p7/r14.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p7/r14.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p7/r14.claim: The envoy must not cause anyone to discover them, even unintentionally; the source calls him the cause of their being noticed.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p7/r14.anchor: ولا يفعلن ما يؤدي إلى الشعر بنا من غير قصد منه فسمى ذلك اشعارا منه بهم

QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20/r1.claim: Baʿath means movement from stillness; here God awakened the youths in the same clothes and condition as before sleep.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20/r2.speaker: شاعر
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20/r2.claim: An unnamed poet uses baʿath for waking young men at dawn.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20/r3.claim: The lām in li-yatasaʾalu is a consequence lām, not a purpose: their awakening resulted in their questioning, as in 28:8.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20/r3.anchor: واللام في قوله «ليتساءلوا» لام الصيرورة وهي لام العاقبة

QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20/r4.claim: They entered the cave in the morning and awoke late in the day; their leader, called Tamlikha or Maksalmina, said God knew the duration.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20/r4.anchor: وذلك أنهم دخلوه غدوة وبعثهم الله في آخر النهار

QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas compares their silver currency to the hooves of a young camel.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس: كانت ورقهم كأخفاف الربع

QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20/r6.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وابن عامر والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20/r6.claim: These readers pronounce the rāʾ in waraqikum with kasra; other readers make it still, and both are dialects.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20/r6.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وابن عامر والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم «بورقكم» بكسر الراء

QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20/r7.speaker: أبو عمرو وحمزة وأبو بكر عن عاصم
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20/r7.claim: They read waraqikum with a still rāʾ, removing the kasra as heavy; al-Zajjaj records a form with kasra on wāw.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20/r7.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو وحمزة وأبو بكر عن عاصم «بورقكم» بسكون الراء

QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20/r8.speaker: الغزنوي
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20/r8.claim: The youths awoke hungry, and al-Ghaznawi identifies the dispatched youth Tamlikha as the youngest.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20/r8.anchor: ويروى أنهم انتبهوا جياعا، وأن المبعوث هو تمليخا

QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20/r9.claim: The city was Ephesus, also called Tarsus; its earlier name was Ephesus and it was renamed Tarsus after Islam. Ibn Abbas says their coins bore the current king's image.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20/r9.anchor: والمدينة: أفسوس ويقال هي طرسوس، وكان اسمها في الجاهلية أفسوس

QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas says their silver coins carried the image of the king of their time.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20/r10.anchor: كان معهم دراهم عليها صورة الملك الذي كان في زمانهم

QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20/r11.claim: Azka food means meat slaughtered lawfully because townspeople sacrificed in the name of idols; Ibn Abbas also says most inhabitants were Magians.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20/r11.anchor: أحل ذبيحة لأن أهل بلدهم كانوا يذبحون على اسم الصنم

QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20/r12.claim: Other readings of azka are more blessed, tastier, or cheaper; they may have asked for enough food for several people, with rice, raisins, or dates proposed.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20/r13.claim: Rizqan means food; let the delegate act discreetly in town and tell nobody, lest discovery expose the rest of the youths.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20/r13.anchor: أي في دخول المدينة وشراء الطعام

QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#2/r1.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن عوف
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#2/r1.claim: A Bukhari report says Abd al-Rahman contracted with Umayya ibn Khalaf to protect each other's dependents in Mecca and Medina; Umayya objected to the name al-Rahman.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#2/r1.anchor: كاتبت أمية بن خلف كتابا بأن يحفظني في صاغيتي بمكة وأحفظه

QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#2/r2.speaker: الأصمعي
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#2/r2.claim: Al-Asmaʿi explains saghiya as a man's adherents who incline toward him, from the verb meaning to incline.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#2/r2.anchor: صاغية الرجل الذين يميلون إليه ويأتونه وهو مأخوذ من صغا

QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#2/r3.claim: Agency is a delegated contract allowed because people need help managing affairs and not everyone can handle every task alone.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#2/r3.anchor: الوكالة عقد نيابة، أذن الله سبحانه فيه للحاجة إليه وقيام المصلحة

QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#2/r4.claim: Jurists support agency from this verse, 9:60, 12:93, and many hadiths, including the report of Urwa al-Bariqi.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#2/r4.anchor: وقد استدل علماؤنا على صحتها بآيات من الكتاب، منها هذه الآية

QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#2/r5.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#2/r5.claim: Jabir says he was sent to Khaybar and told by the Prophet to collect fifteen wasqs from his agent, using a hand on the collarbone as proof if asked.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#2/r5.anchor: إذا أتيت وكيلي فخذ منه خمسة عشر وسقا فإن ابتغى منك آية

QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#2/r6.claim: Agency is valid in any right that can be delegated, but not for a usurper or an unlawful act.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#2/r6.anchor: الوكالة جائزة في كل حق تجوز النيابة فيه

QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#2/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#2/r7.claim: Agency in this story arose from fear of discovery; scholars agree that people with an excuse may appoint agents, while most permit healthy present people too.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#2/r7.anchor: الوكالة إنما كانت مع التقية خوف أن يشعر بهم أحد

QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#2/r8.speaker: أبو حنيفة وسحنون
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#2/r8.claim: Abu Hanifa and Sahnun disallow agency for a person present without an excuse; Ibn al-Arabi speculates Sahnun used this against oppressors, while al-Qurtubi permits it for virtuous people.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#2/r8.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة وسحنون: لا تجوز

QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#3/r1.speaker: النبي ﷺ
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#3/r1.claim: In Abu Hurayra's report, the Prophet repaid a camel debt with a better camel, and the creditor praised him; the Prophet said the best people pay best.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#3/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#3/r2.claim: This sound report shows a healthy person present may appoint others: the Prophet authorized his Companions to repay for him, contrary to Abu Hanifa and Sahnun.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#3/r2.anchor: فدل هذا الحديث مع صحته على جواز توكيل الحاضر الصحيح البدن

QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#3/r3.speaker: ابن خويز منداد
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#3/r3.claim: Ibn Khuwayz says the verse supports partnership because the youths shared their money, agency because they sent a buyer, and joint eating despite unequal appetites.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#3/r3.anchor: تضمنت هذه الآية جواز الشركة لأن الورق كان لجميعهم

QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#3/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#3/r4.claim: The school allows a poor person to mix donated food with a rich person's meal and a business agent to mix provisions and eat together.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#3/r4.anchor: وقد قالوا في المضارب يخلط طعامه بطعام غيره

QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#3/r5.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#3/r5.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says the verse does not prove shared partnership because each youth may have given money separately; he relies instead on two hadiths.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#3/r5.anchor: ليس في الآية دليل على ذلك لأنه يحتمل أن يكون كل واحد منهم قد أعطاه منفردا

QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#3/r6.speaker: ابن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#3/r6.claim: Ibn Umar cites the prohibition on taking two dates together without a companion's permission as evidence about shared food.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#3/r6.anchor: نهى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الاقتران إلا أن يستأذن الرجل أخاه

QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#3/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#3/r7.claim: The army-of-khabt report is less decisive because Abu Ubayda may simply have distributed equal portions rather than having everyone share one supply.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#3/r7.anchor: وهذا دون الأول في الظهور لأنه يحتمل أن يكون أبو عبيدة يعطيهم كفافا

QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#4/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#4/r1.claim: The permission to mix with orphans as siblings and the permission to eat together or separately support shared eating; the source cites 2:220 and labels the latter 24:16.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:19-20#4/r1.anchor: ليس عليكم جناح أن تأكلوا جميعا أو أشتاتا

ZAJJAJ:v3p275/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p275/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p275/r1.claim: Wariq has four vowel patterns, with kasra on wāw the least acceptable; qāf may assimilate into kāf.
ZAJJAJ:v3p275/r1.anchor: فيها أربعة أوجه - بفتح الواو وكسر الراء، وبورقكم بتسكين الراء

ZAJJAJ:v3p275/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p275/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p275/r2.claim: أيها is nominative as a topic meaning which inhabitants of the city; أزكى is its predicate and طعاما a specification.
ZAJJAJ:v3p275/r2.anchor: (أيها) مرفوع بالابتداء، ومعنى (أيها أزكى طعاما) أي أي أهلها

ZAJJAJ:v3p275/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p275/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p275/r3.claim: أزكى طعاما may mean lawful food, since most townspeople were Magians who did not properly slaughter animals, or food not obtained unlawfully.
ZAJJAJ:v3p275/r3.anchor: وقيل: إن تأويل (أزكى طعاما) أحل طعاما،

ZAJJAJ:v3p275/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p275/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p275/r4.claim: A second interpretation is food not taken by usurpation or from an illicit source.
ZAJJAJ:v3p275/r4.anchor: وقيل: (أزكى طعاما) أي طعاما لم يؤخذ من غصب،

ZAJJAJ:v3p276/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p276/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p276/r1.claim: In فليأتكم, the lām is read with sukūn; kasra is permitted.
ZAJJAJ:v3p276/r1.anchor: وفليأتكم - بإسكان اللام وكسرها - والقراءة بإسكان اللام.

ZAJJAJ:v3p276/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p276/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p276/r2.claim: ولا يشعرن بكم means let no one know of you; if the messenger is discovered, he should not expose his companions to danger.
ZAJJAJ:v3p276/r2.anchor: قيل لا يعلمن بكم، أي إن ظهر عليه فلا يوقعن إخوانه

RAZI-FULL:v21p87/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p87/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p87/r1.claim: Their awakening was like revival from sleep resembling death; they had remained alive without food or drink, and were turned over, so God revived them to question one another about their stay.
RAZI-FULL:v21p87/r1.anchor: فكذلك بعثناهم أي أحييناهم من تلك النومة التي تشبه الموت

RAZI-FULL:v21p87/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p87/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p87/r2.claim: Their questioning can itself be an intended purpose: it disclosed extraordinary aspects of God's power, and such disclosure is desirable for its own sake.

RAZI-FULL:v21p87/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p87/r3.speaker: المفسرون
RAZI-FULL:v21p87/r3.claim: Commentators say they entered the cave in the morning and awoke near day's end, explaining why they guessed a day or part of one.
RAZI-FULL:v21p87/r3.anchor: قال المفسرون إنهم دخلوا الكهف غدوة وبعثهم الله في آخر النهار

RAZI-FULL:v21p87/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p87/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v21p87/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the speaker who returned the duration to God as their leader Yamlikhā, who inferred from their changed hair, nails, and faces that much time had passed.
RAZI-FULL:v21p87/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس هو رئيسهم يمليخا رد علم ذلك إلى الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v21p87/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p87/r5.speaker: أبو عمرو وحمزة وأبو بكر عن عاصم
RAZI-FULL:v21p87/r5.claim: Abū ʿAmr, Ḥamza, and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim read wariqikum with sukūn on rāʾ and fatḥa on wāw; Ibn Kathīr reads kasra on rāʾ and assimilates qāf into kāf.
RAZI-FULL:v21p87/r5.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو وحمزة وأبو بكر عن عاصم بورقكم ساكنة الراء مفتوحة الواو

RAZI-FULL:v21p87/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p87/r6.speaker: ابن محيصن
RAZI-FULL:v21p87/r6.claim: Ibn Muḥayṣin's reading combines kasra on wāw with sukūn on rāʾ and assimilation, which Rāzī rejects because it creates two consecutive sukūns.
RAZI-FULL:v21p87/r6.anchor: وعن ابن محيصن أنه كسر الواو وأسكن الراء وأدغم القاف في الكاف

RAZI-FULL:v21p87/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p87/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p87/r7.claim: Wariq means silver, coined or uncoined; a report about ʿArfaja using a silver nose supports the uncoined sense, and several vowel forms are attested.
RAZI-FULL:v21p87/r7.anchor: والورق اسم للفضة سواء كانت مضروبة أم لا

RAZI-FULL:v21p87/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p87/r8.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v21p87/r8.claim: Al-Farrāʾ lists the forms waraqu, warqu, and wariqu, and calls kasra on wāw the least good form.
RAZI-FULL:v21p87/r8.anchor: ذكره الفراء والزجاج قال الفراء وكسر الواو أردؤها

RAZI-FULL:v21p87/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p87/r9.speaker: الأزهري
RAZI-FULL:v21p87/r9.claim: Al-Azharī says riqqa, another word for silver, derives from wariq through the pattern of ṣila and ʿida.
RAZI-FULL:v21p87/r9.anchor: قال الأزهري أصله ورق مثل صلة وعدة

RAZI-FULL:v21p87/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p87/r10.speaker: المفسرون
RAZI-FULL:v21p87/r10.claim: Commentators say the youths carried coins bearing the image of the king of their time and that their city was what is now called Tarsus.
RAZI-FULL:v21p87/r10.anchor: كانت معهم دراهم عليها صورة الملك الذي كان في زمانهم يعني بالمدينة التي يقال لها اليوم طرسوس

RAZI-FULL:v21p87/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p87/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p87/r11.claim: The episode shows that taking steps to secure food is important and does not negate reliance on God.
RAZI-FULL:v21p87/r11.anchor: وهذه الآية تدل على أن السعي في إمساك الزاد أمر مهم مشروع وأنه لا يبطل التوكل

RAZI-FULL:v21p87/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p87/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v21p87/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the purest food as lawful slaughter, since most inhabitants were Magians, though some secretly believed.
RAZI-FULL:v21p87/r12.anchor: يريد ما حل من الذبائح لأن عامة أهل بلدهم

RAZI-FULL:v21p87/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p87/r13.speaker: مجاهد
RAZI-FULL:v21p87/r13.claim: Mujāhid says they sought food farthest from the tyrant's injustice; other glosses understand the phrase as tastiest or cheapest.

RAZI-FULL:v21p87/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p87/r14.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v21p87/r14.claim: Al-Zajjāj parses ayyuhā as subject, azkā as its predicate, and ṭaʿāman as a specification.

RAZI-FULL:v21p87/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p87/r15.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p87/r15.claim: The emissary should act discreetly while entering the city and buying food, and tell nobody where the youths are.
RAZI-FULL:v21p87/r15.anchor: أي يكون ذلك في سر وكتمان يعني دخول المدينة وشراء الطعام

ASAD-NOTES:18:19#n23/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:18:19#n23/r1.speaker: most commentators
ASAD-NOTES:18:19#n23/r1.claim: Most commentators take li in li-yatasa'alu to express purpose: so that the youths might ask one another.
ASAD-NOTES:18:19#n23/r1.anchor: which most commentators take to mean "so that they might ask one another"

ASAD-NOTES:18:19#n23/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:18:19#n23/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:18:19#n23/r2.claim: Asad instead reads li as lam al-aqibah, marking causal sequence, which he renders as and they began to ask.
ASAD-NOTES:18:19#n23/r2.anchor: li in li-yatasa'alu (which most commentators take to mean "so that they might ask one another") is not a particle

STUDYQURAN:18:19/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:19/r1.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:18:19/r1.claim: The youths awoke after a shepherd opened the cave while seeking shelter for his flock from rain.
STUDYQURAN:18:19/r1.anchor: the youths awoke after their cave was discovered by a shepherd looking for a place to shelter his flock from the rain. When he cleared the entrance of the cave, the youths awoke (Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:18:19/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:19/r2.speaker: IK, Ṭ, Z
STUDYQURAN:18:19/r2.claim: Some say they estimated a day because they entered the cave in the morning and awoke at sunset.
STUDYQURAN:18:19/r2.anchor: they estimated they had passed a day, since they entered the cave in the morning and awoke at sunset (IK, Ṭ, Z)

STUDYQURAN:18:19/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:19/r3.speaker: R, Z
STUDYQURAN:18:19/r3.claim: Others say they noticed their long hair and nails before concluding that God knew best how long they had slept.
STUDYQURAN:18:19/r3.anchor: only upon seeing the length of their hair and nails did they say, Your Lord knows best how long you have tarried (R, Z)

STUDYQURAN:18:19/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:19/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:19/r4.claim: Their one-day estimate resembles the man awakened after a hundred years and Quranic accounts of people thinking their wait before resurrection was short.
STUDYQURAN:18:19/r4.anchor: their estimation of having tarried a day is identical to that made by a man who had doubted the resurrection

STUDYQURAN:18:19/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:19/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:19/r5.claim: The parallel reactions connect the Cave story symbolically with death, resurrection, and the intervening barzakh.
STUDYQURAN:18:19/r5.anchor: the close symbolic connection of this story to death, resurrection, and the intermediate state, or barzakh, between them

STUDYQURAN:18:19/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:19/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:19/r6.claim: The chosen youth carried a silver dirham stamped with the oppressive king’s image and was told to buy food discreetly to avoid persecution.
STUDYQURAN:18:19/r6.anchor: a silver dirham bearing the imprint of the oppressive king of their own time, and to enter the city in order to purchase food; but he was to do this discreetly

STUDYQURAN:18:19/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:19/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:19/r7.claim: The old coin exposed the youth; centuries had passed and the city was ruled by the righteous king Tīdhusīs, or Theodocius.
STUDYQURAN:18:19/r7.anchor: the people were amazed to see the old coin. They informed the youth that centuries had passed. They were now ruled by a righteous king, Tīdhusīs (Theodocius; Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:18:19/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:19/r11.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:18:19/r11.claim: When the youth rejoined the others, they returned to deep sleep; the king and townspeople later found their bodies perfectly preserved.
STUDYQURAN:18:19/r11.anchor: he was instantly returned to his deep sleep, as were his companions. The king and the townsfolk later entered and found them in a state of bodily perfection, without any sign of decomposition (Ṭ)

ASAD-NOTES:18:19#n24/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:18:19#n24/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:18:19#n24/r1.claim: The matching question and answer in 2:259 link both allegories to God's power to create life, end it, and resurrect.
ASAD-NOTES:18:19#n24/r1.anchor: exactly the same question is asked and exactly the same wondering answer is given

ASAD-NOTES:18:19#n24/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:18:19#n24/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:18:19#n24/r2.claim: The story also exposes the deceptive, earthbound human conception of time.
ASAD-NOTES:18:19#n24/r2.anchor: the deceptive, purely earthbound character of the human concept of "time".

ASAD-NOTES:18:19#n25/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:18:19#n25/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:18:19#n25/r1.claim: Some sleepers understood that the interval had no independent reality, as with death and resurrection; this explains the two viewpoints in verse 12.
ASAD-NOTES:18:19#n25/r1.anchor: the lapse of time between their "falling asleep" and their "awakening" had no reality of its own

TAB-FULL:v15p161/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p161/r5.speaker: عمرو
TAB-FULL:v15p161/r5.claim: The youths sent one of their number to Ephesus with an old coin; the townspeople recognized its age, consulted the king and records, and rejoiced when they learned the youths' story.
TAB-FULL:v15p161/r5.anchor: ثم أخرج درهما، فنظروا إليه فأنكروه، وأنكروا الدرهم، وقالوا: من أين لك هذا؟

TAB-FULL:v15p196/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p196/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p196/r1.claim: The youths question one another because they find their long sleep strange; some estimate a day or part of one, believing that is how long they slept.
TAB-FULL:v15p196/r1.anchor: ظنا منهم أن ذلك كذلك كان

TAB-FULL:v15p196/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p196/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p196/r2.claim: The others defer the matter to God, saying that their Lord knows best how long they remained asleep.
TAB-FULL:v15p196/r2.anchor: فقال الآخرون: {ربكم أعلم بما لبثتم} [الكهف: 19] فسلموا العلم إلى الله

TAB-FULL:v15p197/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p197/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p197/r1.claim: The youths send one of their number to their former city, Ephesus, to buy food because they have awakened hungry.

TAB-FULL:v15p197/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p197/r2.speaker: وهب بن منبه
TAB-FULL:v15p197/r2.claim: Wahb says a shepherd opened the cave for sheltering sheep from rain; the youths revived the next morning and sent one with old silver to buy food, revealing their long sleep to a righteous king.
TAB-FULL:v15p197/r2.anchor: أنه سمع وهب بن منبه، يقول: إنهم غبروا، يعني الفتية من أصحاب الكهف بعد ما بني عليهم باب الكهف

TAB-FULL:v15p197/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p197/r3.speaker: وهب بن منبه
TAB-FULL:v15p197/r3.claim: When the messenger led the king and people to the cave, terror kept them from entering; they later built a church or mosque there for prayer.
TAB-FULL:v15p197/r3.anchor: فبنوا عندهم كنيسة، اتخذوها مسجدا يصلون فيه

TAB-FULL:v15p199/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p199/r1.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v15p199/r1.claim: Ikrima reports that Christian youths, sons of Roman kings, withdrew from their people and slept until a Muslim community and king arose, then sought God's sign amid a dispute about bodily resurrection.
TAB-FULL:v15p199/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، عن عكرمة، قال: كان أصحاب الكهف أبناء ملوك الروم، رزقهم الله الإسلام

TAB-FULL:v15p199/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p199/r2.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v15p199/r2.claim: The awakened envoy's old coin exposed the era he came from, and the king presented the youths as a sign that body and soul are resurrected together.
TAB-FULL:v15p199/r2.anchor: فهذا رجل من قوم فلان، يعني ملكهم الذي مضى، فقال الفتى: انطلقوا بي إلى أصحابي

TAB-FULL:v15p199/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p199/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v15p199/r3.claim: Qatada says that when people entered the cave they found bodies without souls, and the king called them a sign from God.
TAB-FULL:v15p199/r3.anchor: فإذا أجساد لا ينكرون منها شيئا، غير أنها لا أرواح فيها، فقال الملك: هذه آية بعثها الله لكم

TAB-FULL:v15p199/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p199/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p199/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas, passing the cave on campaign with Habib ibn Maslama, says the youths' bones had already vanished more than three hundred years later.
TAB-FULL:v15p199/r4.anchor: وعن ابن عباس، كان قد غزا مع حبيب بن مسلمة، فمروا بالكهف، فإذا فيه عظام

TAB-FULL:v15p200/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p200/r1.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v15p200/r1.claim: Ibn Ishaq's account places the awakening under the righteous king Theodosius, whose reign lasted sixty-eight years and whose people split over belief in the Hour.
TAB-FULL:v15p200/r1.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، فيما ذكر من حديث أصحاب الكهف، قال: ثم ملك أهل تلك البلاد رجل صالح يقال له تيذوسيس

TAB-FULL:v15p200/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p200/r2.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v15p200/r2.claim: The disputants included believers and deniers who claimed only souls, not bodies, would be raised and forgot scripture; falsehood gained ground over the believers.
TAB-FULL:v15p200/r2.anchor: ومنهم من يكذب، فكبر ذلك على الملك الصالح تيذوسيس، وبكى إلى الله وتضرع إليه

TAB-FULL:v15p200/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p200/r3.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v15p200/r3.claim: Theodosius withdraws, wears sackcloth, sits on ashes, and prays in grief for a sign to resolve the dispute.
TAB-FULL:v15p200/r3.anchor: دخل بيته فأغلقه عليه، ولبس مسحا وجعل تحته رمادا

TAB-FULL:v15p200/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p200/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p200/r4.claim: God intends the youths' appearance to establish the Hour and bodily resurrection as truth, answer Theodosius' prayer, preserve his faith and rule, and gather dispersed believers.
TAB-FULL:v15p200/r4.anchor: ثم إن الرحمن الرحيم الذي يكره هلكة العباد، أراد أن يظهر على الفتية أصحاب الكهف

TAB-FULL:v15p200/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p200/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p200/r5.claim: God inspires Olyas to remove the stones from the cave entrance for a sheep pen; terror keeps people at a distance while the youths sit up revived, greet each other, and pray unchanged.
TAB-FULL:v15p200/r5.anchor: فاستأجر عاملين، فجعلا ينزعان تلك الحجارة

TAB-FULL:v15p202/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p202/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p202/r1.claim: After prayer, the youths ask Yemliha what happened and estimate their sleep as a day or part of one; he says Deqianus seeks them and will force sacrifice or kill them.
TAB-FULL:v15p202/r1.anchor: فقال لهم يمليخا: افتقدتم والتمستم بالمدينة، وهو يريد أن يؤتى بكم اليوم

TAB-FULL:v15p202/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p202/r2.speaker: مكسلمينا
TAB-FULL:v15p202/r2.claim: Maksalimina urges them to face death without abandoning belief in God or the life after death.
TAB-FULL:v15p202/r2.anchor: فقال لهم مكسلمينا: يا إخوتاه اعلموا أنكم ملاقون، فلا تكفروا بعد إيمانكم

TAB-FULL:v15p202/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p202/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p202/r3.claim: They instruct Yemliha to go secretly to town, learn what is said about them, and bring more food; he takes their old coins and sees the cave entrance has been unsealed.
TAB-FULL:v15p202/r3.anchor: وأخذ ورقا من نفقتهم التي كانت معهم، التي ضربت بطابع دقينوس الملك

TAB-FULL:v15p202/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p202/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p202/r4.claim: The youths think they have slept only their usual night and still believe Deqianus is seeking them, unaware that 309 years have passed.
TAB-FULL:v15p202/r4.anchor: أن استيقظوا ثلاث مائة وتسع سنين

TAB-FULL:v15p203/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p203/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p203/r1.claim: Yemliha sees Christian signs displayed at the city gates and hears people openly invoking Jesus, unlike the persecution he remembers; the changed city leaves him bewildered.
TAB-FULL:v15p203/r1.anchor: فرأى فوق ظهر الباب علامة تكون لأهل الإيمان، إذا كان ظاهرا فيها

TAB-FULL:v15p203/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p203/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p203/r2.claim: He asks a local youth the city's name and learns it is Ephesus, yet fears he has lost his mind and tries to leave unseen.
TAB-FULL:v15p203/r2.anchor: فقال له: ما اسم هذه المدينة يا فتى؟ قال: اسمها أفسوس

TAB-FULL:v15p203/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p203/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p203/r3.claim: When Yemliha offers an ancient coin for food, sellers pass it around and suspect he has found a buried treasure from long ago.
TAB-FULL:v15p203/r3.anchor: ثم جعلوا يتطارحونها بينهم من رجل إلى رجل، ويتعجبون منها

TAB-FULL:v15p204/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p204/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p204/r1.claim: The townspeople accuse Yemliha of hiding a treasure, threaten to take him to the ruler, bind him, and parade him through the streets as a stranger.
TAB-FULL:v15p204/r1.anchor: أخذوا كساءه فطوقوه في عنقه، ثم جعلوا يقودونه في سكك المدينة ملببا

TAB-FULL:v15p204/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p204/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p204/r2.claim: They bring him to the city's two righteous governors, Arius and Astius; he believes he is being taken to Deqianus and cries to God for help.
TAB-FULL:v15p204/r2.anchor: وهما رجلان صالحان، كان اسم أحدهما أريوس، واسم الآخر أسطيوس

TAB-FULL:v15p204/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p204/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p204/r3.claim: Yemliha fears separation from his brothers and recalls their pledge never to forsake faith or one another in life or death.
TAB-FULL:v15p204/r3.anchor: وقد كنا تواثقنا أن لا نفترق في حياة ولا موت أبدا

TAB-FULL:v15p206/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p206/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p206/r1.claim: The city they fled was Ephesus, and the youths woke from their long sleep hungry, so they asked for food.
TAB-FULL:v15p206/r1.anchor: ذلك الذي يحدث به يمليخا نفسه فيما أخبر أصحابه

TAB-FULL:v15p206/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p206/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p206/r2.claim: When Yamlīkha returned with the old coin, two city officials suspected he had found a treasure; he said it was his fathers’ currency and could not explain his situation.
TAB-FULL:v15p206/r2.anchor: هذا الورق يشهد عليك أنك قد وجدت كنزا

TAB-FULL:v15p206/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p206/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p206/r3.claim: No one recognized Yamlīkha or his father; some called him mad, while the officials accused him of lying and threatened torture until he confessed.
TAB-FULL:v15p206/r3.anchor: ولا أباه، فقال له أحدهما: أنت رجل كذاب

TAB-FULL:v15p206/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p206/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p206/r4.claim: Asked about Daqyanus, the townspeople said no such man lived and that the king had died long ago; Yamlīkha realized centuries had passed.
TAB-FULL:v15p206/r4.anchor: ليس على وجه الأرض رجل اسمه دقينوس، ولم يكن إلا ملك

TAB-FULL:v15p206/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p206/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p206/r5.claim: Yamlīkha said he had seen Daqyanus enter Ephesus the previous evening, asked the officials to see his companions, and Areus recognized a possible sign from God.
TAB-FULL:v15p206/r5.anchor: يا قوم لعل هذه آية من آيات الله جعلها لكم على يدي هذا الفتى

TAB-FULL:v15p206/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p206/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p206/r6.claim: Areus, Astius, and the townspeople, both prominent and ordinary, accompanied Yamlīkha toward the cave to see the sleepers.
TAB-FULL:v15p206/r6.anchor: فانطلق معه أريوس وأسطيوس، وانطلق معهم أهل المدينة

TAB-FULL:v15p208/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p208/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p208/r1.claim: When Yamlīkha delayed, his companions feared Daqyanus had captured him; hearing horses, they prayed, exchanged farewells, and expected to face the tyrant.
TAB-FULL:v15p208/r1.anchor: ظنوا أنه قد أخذ فذهب به إلى ملكهم دقينوس الذي هربوا منه

TAB-FULL:v15p208/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p208/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p208/r2.claim: They found Areus and the townspeople at the cave instead; Yamlīkha told the youths what happened, and they understood God had awakened them as a sign of resurrection.
TAB-FULL:v15p208/r2.anchor: فعرفوا عند ذلك أنهم كانوا نياما بأمر الله ذلك الزمان كله، وإنما أوقظوا ليكونوا آية للناس

TAB-FULL:v15p211/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p211/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن عبيد بن عمير
TAB-FULL:v15p211/r1.claim: The youths were raised under a Muslim king, hungry; one judged they had slept a day or less, then deferred the true duration to God and went to buy food with old coins.
TAB-FULL:v15p211/r1.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عبيد بن عمير، قال: بعثهم الله يعني الفتية أصحاب الكهف

TAB-FULL:v15p211/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p211/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن عبيد بن عمير
TAB-FULL:v15p211/r2.claim: The old coins dated from a king three hundred and nine years earlier; the merchant took Yamlīkha to the Muslim king, and the account matched an archived tablet.
TAB-FULL:v15p211/r2.anchor: هذه الورق من ضرب فلان بن فلان منذ ثلاثمائة وتسع سنين أنت أصبت كنزا

TAB-FULL:v15p211/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p211/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p211/r5.claim: Medinan and some Iraqi readers pronounce ورقكم with fatḥa on wāw and kasra on rāʾ; most Kufan and Basran readers make rāʾ quiescent.
TAB-FULL:v15p211/r5.anchor: فقرأ ذلك عامة قراء أهل المدينة وبعض العراقيين {بورقكم هذه} [الكهف: 19] بفتح الواو وكسر الراء والقاف

TAB-FULL:v15p211/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p211/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p211/r6.claim: Some Meccan readers kasrate rāʾ and assimilate qāf into kāf; all readings carry the same meaning and reflect known Arabic forms.
TAB-FULL:v15p211/r6.anchor: وقرأه بعض المكيين بكسر الراء، وإدغام القاف في الكاف، وكل هذه القراءات متفقات المعاني

TAB-FULL:v15p211/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p211/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p211/r7.claim: The original form is ورق with wāw fatḥa and rāʾ and qāf kasra, so al-Ṭabarī prefers that reading while accepting the others as sound forms of Arabic.
TAB-FULL:v15p211/r7.anchor: غير أن الأصل في ذلك فتح الواو وكسر الراء والقاف

TAB-FULL:v15p212/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p212/r1.speaker: مقاتل
TAB-FULL:v15p212/r1.claim: A report transmitted from Muqātil identifies the youth sent with the coins as Yamlīkh.
TAB-FULL:v15p212/r1.anchor: عن مقاتل، {فابعثوا أحدكم بورقكم هذه} [الكهف: 19] اسمه يمليخ

TAB-FULL:v15p213/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p213/r1.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v15p213/r1.claim: ʿIkrima interprets أزكى طعاما as asking which resident has the most food.
TAB-FULL:v15p213/r1.anchor: عن أبي حصين، عن عكرمة، {أيها أزكى طعاما} [الكهف: 19] قال: أكثر

TAB-FULL:v15p213/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p213/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v15p213/r2.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr interprets أزكى طعاما as asking which food is more lawful.
TAB-FULL:v15p213/r2.anchor: عن أبي حصين، عن سعيد بن جبير: {أيها أزكى طعاما} [الكهف: 19] قال: أحل

TAB-FULL:v15p213/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p213/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v15p213/r3.claim: Qatāda gives the sense as asking which food is better.
TAB-FULL:v15p213/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، في قوله: {أزكى طعاما} [الكهف: 19] قال: خير طعاما

TAB-FULL:v15p213/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p213/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p213/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers lawful and pure food: requiring the best makes sense whether a seller has much or little, and lawful good food outweighs abundant unlawful food.
TAB-FULL:v15p213/r4.anchor: وأولى الأقوال عندي في ذلك بالصواب: قول من قال: معنى ذلك: أحل وأطهر

TAB-FULL:v15p213/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p213/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p213/r5.claim: The more-food interpretation draws on Arabic usage where zakā can mean increase; an unnamed poem uses أزكى to mean more, but al-Ṭabarī says that does not decide the verse’s sense.

TAB-FULL:v15p213/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p213/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p213/r6.claim: أيها is grammatically attached to the city but means its inhabitants, since listeners understand that the food belongs to people.
TAB-FULL:v15p213/r6.anchor: وقيل: {فلينظر أيها} [الكهف: 19] فأضيف إلى كناية المدينة، والمراد بها أهلها

TAB-FULL:v15p213/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p213/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p213/r7.claim: The youths may have meant which food was lawful because they had left an idolatrous people and would not permit themselves to eat their sacrificial meat.
TAB-FULL:v15p213/r7.anchor: من أجل أنهم كانوا فارقوا قومهم وهم أهل أوثان

TAB-FULL:v15p214/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p214/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن عبيد بن عمير
TAB-FULL:v15p214/r1.claim: رزق means food or sustenance to eat.
TAB-FULL:v15p214/r1.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عبيد بن عمير، {فليأتكم برزق منه} [الكهف: 19] قال: بطعام

TAB-FULL:v15p214/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p214/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p214/r2.claim: The messenger should act gently and cautiously while shopping, traveling, and entering the city, and ensure no one learns about the youths.
TAB-FULL:v15p214/r2.anchor: وقوله: {وليتلطف} [الكهف: 19] يقول: وليترفق في شرائه ما يشتري، وفي طريقه ودخوله المدينة

TABATABAI:18:23/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:23/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:23/r4.claim: The cave sleepers mirror humanity absorbed in earthly adornment: people will awaken from worldly life and reckon its long span as a day or part of one.
TABATABAI:18:23/r4.anchor: ليس ذلك كله إلا آية إلهية هي نظيرة ما جرى على أصحاب الكهف

TABATABAI:18:9-26#10/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#10/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#10/r1.claim: Tasāʾul is mutual questioning; waraq is dirhams or silver, coined or uncoined; yuẓhirū ʿalaykum can mean discover or overcome you.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#10/r1.anchor: التساؤل سؤال بعض القوم بعضا، والورق بالفتح فالكسر الدراهم، وقيل هو الفضة

TABATABAI:18:9-26#10/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#10/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#10/r2.claim: “Likewise We awakened them” refers back to their long, remarkable sleep; the questioning was the immediate purpose of waking them.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#10/r2.anchor: كما أنمناهم في الكهف دهرا طويلا على هذا الوضع العجيب المدهش

TABATABAI:18:9-26#10/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#10/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#10/r3.claim: Their despair at the apparent triumph of coercive falsehood parallels the man revived after a century; their awakening shows that time's length does not destroy truth or revive falsehood.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#10/r3.anchor: فأماته الله مائة عام ثم بعثه

TABATABAI:18:9-26#10/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#10/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#10/r4.claim: Earthly life and its events pass like a brief dream, but worldly distraction keeps people from recognizing the truth until death or the end of the world.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#10/r4.anchor: وجدها كطائف في نومة أو سنة في مثل يوم

TABATABAI:18:9-26#10/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#10/r5.speaker: علي عليه السلام
TABATABAI:18:9-26#10/r5.claim: Ali says people are asleep and awaken when they die.

TABATABAI:18:9-26#10/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#10/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#10/r6.claim: Humanity will also awaken when the world's adornment is folded up and the human world is brought to extinction.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#10/r6.anchor: ويوم آخر وهو يوم يطوى فيه بساط الدنيا وزينتها

TABATABAI:18:9-26#11/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#11/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#11/r1.claim: The questioning is the real purpose of awakening and aligns with the purpose stated in 18:12.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#11/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى { ليتساءلوا بينهم } غاية لبعثهم

TABATABAI:18:9-26#11/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#11/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#11/r2.claim: Treating the questioning as only a subordinate purpose lacks textual evidence; treating it as a mere consequence does not answer the objection that it is a small outcome of a great miracle.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#11/r2.anchor: وهذا مع عدم شاهد عليه من جهة اللفظ تكلف ظاهر

TABATABAI:18:9-26#11/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#11/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#11/r3.claim: One youth asked the others how long they had slept, apparently sensing a long interval from the heaviness of their sleep.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#11/r3.anchor: وكأن السائل استشعر طولا في لبثهم مما وجده من لوثة النوم الثقيل

TABATABAI:18:9-26#11/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#11/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#11/r4.claim: “A day or part of a day” is one speaker's uncertain estimate based on the sun's changed position, not a division in which some said a day and others part of one.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#11/r4.anchor: وقد أجاب بمثله شخص واحد بعينه قال تعالى

TABATABAI:18:9-26#12/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#12/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#12/r1.claim: Observed sun, shadows, light, and darkness cannot establish an exact full day; here “day” commonly means slightly more than a night and day.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#12/r1.anchor: الأمور الخارجية التي يستدل بها الإنسان وخاصة من نام ثم انتبه من شمس وظل

TABATABAI:18:9-26#12/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#12/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#12/r2.claim: Saying “your Lord knows” states an epistemic truth: humans know external events only through indicators, while God alone directly encompasses each thing and event.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#12/r2.anchor: فإن الإنسان محجوب عما وراء نفسه لا يملك بإذن الله إلا نفسه

TABATABAI:18:9-26#12/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#12/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#12/r3.claim: The speakers who appeal to God's knowledge show higher monotheistic insight than those who estimate a day; they are a different group, not the factions in 18:12.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#12/r3.anchor: أن القائلين منهم { ربكم أعلم بما لبثتم } كانوا أعلى كعبا في مقام المعرفة

TABATABAI:18:9-26#12/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#12/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#12/r4.claim: The dialogue implies at least seven youths: one asks, and each of two plural replies requires at least three people.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#12/r4.anchor: ومن هنا يستفاد أن القوم كانوا سبعة أو أزيد

TABATABAI:18:9-26#12/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#12/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#12/r5.claim: They propose sending one of their own to buy food; “which one” refers grammatically to the city but means its residents.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#12/r5.anchor: الضمير في { أيها } راجع إلى المدينة والمراد بها أهلها من الكسبة استخداما

TABATABAI:18:9-26#12/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#12/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#12/r6.claim: The requested errand is to obtain food for them to eat, introduced as a proposal to the group.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#12/r6.anchor: وفيه أمر أو عرض لهم أن يرسلوا رسولا منهم إلى المدينة ليشتري لهم طعاما

TABATABAI:18:9-26#13/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#13/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#13/r1.claim: Zakiy food may mean good, lawful, or pure food; the comparative form favors the first sense.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#13/r1.anchor: وزكاء الطعام كونه طيبا وقيل كونه حلالا وقيل كونه طاهرا

TABATABAI:18:9-26#13/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#13/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#13/r2.claim: In “bring you sustenance from it,” the pronoun most naturally refers to the food; taking it to refer to the silver is remote and requires an extra implied pronoun.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#13/r2.anchor: والضمير في { منه } للطعام المفهوم من الكلام

TABATABAI:18:9-26#13/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#13/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#13/r3.claim: Talaṭṭuf is acting gently and showing care; in context the envoy should deal smoothly with residents to avoid a quarrel that reveals them.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#13/r3.anchor: والمراد على ما يعطيه السياق ليتكلف اللطف مع أهل المدينة في ذهابه ومجيئه

TABATABAI:18:9-26#13/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#13/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#13/r4.claim: A broader reading of tact as general caution in transactions is not supported by the explicit following clause.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#13/r4.anchor: وقيل المعنى ليتكلف اللطف في المعاملة وإطلاق الكلام يدفعه

TABATABAI:18:9-26#13/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#13/r5.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:18:9-26#13/r5.claim: Al-Rāghib traces ẓuhūr to visibility, from which the word extends to learning of something, finding it, or prevailing over it.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#13/r5.anchor: والكلمة على ما ذكره الراغب مأخوذة من الظهر بمعنى الجارحة

TABATABAI:18:9-26#13/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#13/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#13/r6.claim: The author prefers “discover your location” for yuẓhirū ʿalaykum because it covers how the powerful townspeople could then capture and overpower the youths.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#13/r6.anchor: وظاهر السياق أن يكون { يظهروا عليكم } بمعنى يطلعوا عليكم ويعلموا بمكانكم

TABATABAI:18:9-26#13/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#13/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#13/r7.claim: The choice of stoning signals the townspeople's hostility to the youths' faith and the likelihood of a collective attack.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#13/r7.anchor: وفي اختيار الرجم على غيره من أصناف القتل إشعار بأن أهل المدينة عامة كانوا يعادونهم لدينهم

TABATABAI:18:9-26#13/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#13/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#13/r8.claim: “Return you into their creed” uses a verb carrying the sense of insertion, hence the preposition fi rather than ilā.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#13/r8.anchor: الإعادة مضمن معنى الإدخال ولذا عدي بفي دون إلى

TABATABAI:18:9-26#13/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#13/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#13/r9.claim: Being returned would likely mean enforced participation in idol worship and loss of their true religious practices, not only verbal assent.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#13/r9.anchor: أن لا يقنع القوم بمجرد اعترافهم بحقية الملة صورة دون أن يثقوا بصدقهم في الاعتراف

TABATABAI:18:9-26#14/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#14/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#14/r1.claim: A captive or weak person trapped in an unbelieving society may comply under coercion while keeping faith inwardly, as 16:106 and 3:28 allow.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#14/r1.anchor: وقد قال تعالى إلا من أكره وقلبه مطمئن بالإيمان

TABATABAI:18:9-26#14/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#14/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#14/r2.claim: Someone free to leave who voluntarily enters a hostile society and loses the ability to profess faith has wronged himself; 4:97 rebukes those who claim they were helpless despite a spacious earth.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#14/r2.anchor: وأما من كان بنجوة منهم وهو حر في اعتقاده وعمله ثم ألقى بنفسه في مهلكة الضلال

TABATABAI:18:9-26#14/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#14/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#14/r3.claim: The author rejects proposed harmonizations: coerced apostasy leading to Satanic influence, return by invitation alone, or a period when dissimulation was forbidden lack textual support.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#14/r3.anchor: وقد أجابوا عن الإشكال بوجوه أخر غير مقنعة منها أن الإكراه على الكفر

TABATABAI:18:9-26#14/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#14/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#14/r4.claim: The exchange portrays close fellowship: they share religious insight, delegate equally, use communal money, advise tact, and care for one another's safety.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#14/r4.anchor: وسياق ما حكي من محاورتهم أعني قوله { لبثتم } إلى تمام الآيتين سياق عجيب دال على كمال تحابهم

TABATABAI:18:9-26#15/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#15/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#15/r1.claim: The emphatic phrase “your silver, this” is unusual for a food errand; the coin's age—three centuries—caused the youths to be recognized.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#15/r1.anchor: ولعلها إنما ذكرت في الآية مع خصوصية الإشارة لأنها كانت هي السبب لظهور أمرهم

TABATABAI:18:9-26#27/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#27/r3.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:18:9-26#27/r3.claim: They entered the cave with the dog and slept until that king and city disappeared, then awoke in a new era and initially thought they had slept a day or part of one.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#27/r3.anchor: فناموا حتى أهلك الله ذلك الملك وأهل المدينة وذهب ذلك الزمان وجاء زمان آخر وقوم آخرون

TABATABAI:18:9-26#27/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#27/r4.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:18:9-26#27/r4.claim: One youth went for food with old currency, found a changed city and mutually unintelligible people, and was questioned after asking for provisions.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#27/r4.anchor: فرأى مدينة بخلاف التي عهدها ورأى قوما بخلاف أولئك لم يعرفهم ولم يعرفوا لغته

TABATABAI:18:26#4/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:26#4/r3.speaker: أبو جعفر
TABATABAI:18:26#4/r3.claim: A report from Abu Jaʿfar says the youths were money changers.
TABATABAI:18:26#4/r3.anchor: وفي الدر المنثور أخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن أبي جعفر قال كان أصحاب الكهف صيارفة

TABATABAI:18:26#4/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:26#4/r4.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:18:26#4/r4.claim: Al-Sadiq distinguishes money changers in speech from dealers in coins.
TABATABAI:18:26#4/r4.anchor: فقال كانوا صيارفة كلام ولم يكونوا صيارفة دراهم

TABATABAI:18:9-26#30/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#30/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TABATABAI:18:9-26#30/r2.claim: A later just king’s era began before God awakened them; they disputed whether they slept a day or longer, then sent one with an old coin to buy food, exposing the changed city and era.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#30/r2.anchor: ثم إن ذلك الملك ذهب وجاء ملك آخر فعبد الله وترك تلك الأوثان وعدل في الناس فبعثهم الله

TABATABAI:18:9-26#30/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#30/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TABATABAI:18:9-26#30/r3.claim: The coin seller alerted officials, who identified the youths from the tablet; the messenger entered the cave while the crowd could not find or enter it, and they built a mosque to pray and seek forgiveness for them.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#30/r3.anchor: فقالوا لنتخذن عليهم مسجدا فاتخذوا عليهم مسجدا يصلون عليهم ويستغفرون لهم

TABATABAI:18:9-26#31/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#31/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#31/r3.claim: The report’s claim that some said two days or more conflicts with the Quran’s day or part of a day and with ordinary evidence; differing about duration is a disagreement in judgment, not blameworthy dissent in action.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#31/r3.anchor: وأما احتمال اليومين وأزيد فمما لا سبيل إليه ولا شاهد يشهد عليه عادة

TABATABAI:18:9-26#32/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#32/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#32/r10.claim: The cave story circulated in detailed reports from al-Qummī, Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿIkrima, Mujāhid, Ibn Isḥāq, Wahb ibn Munabbih, and al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr, among others.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#32/r10.anchor: وردت قصة الكهف مفصلة كاملة في عدة روايات عن الصحابة والتابعين وأئمه أهل البيت

TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r1.claim: The transmitted accounts disagree even on major features, while reports about dates, rulers, lineage, appearance, names, and the title أصحاب الرقيم diverge still more.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r1.anchor: من الاختلاف في متونها بحيث لا تكاد تتفق في جهة بارزه من جهات القصة

TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r2.claim: One cause is the story’s prominence among People of the Book: Quraysh learned it from them, and its Christian images and monuments spread it widely, so communities reshaped it to fit their beliefs.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r2.anchor: أن القصة مما اعتنت به أهل الكتاب كما يستفاد من رواياتها أن قريشا تلقتها عنهم

TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r3.claim: A second cause is Muslims’ broad collection of outside reports, especially through converts such as Wahb ibn Munabbih and Kaʿb al-Aḥbār; later transmitters treated such material as prophetic reports.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r3.anchor: اختلط بهم قوم من علماء أهل الكتاب دخلوا في الإسلام كوهب بن منبه وكعب الأحبار

TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r4.claim: The Qurʾān selects key lessons that serve guidance instead of supplying a complete historical account; it is a book of guidance, not history.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r4.anchor: فما كتاب الله بكتاب تاريخ وإنما هو كتاب هدى

TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r5.claim: The Qurʾānic narrative first shows the youths’ truth-bearing withdrawal and long sleep, then their awakening and exchange that exposes them, and finally their discovery and the mosque built over them.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r5.anchor: أورد أولا شطرا من محاورتهم يشير إلى معنى قيامهم لله وثباتهم على كلمة الحق

TABATABAI:18:9-26#34/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#34/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#34/r1.claim: The Qurʾān omits names, ancestry, birth, upbringing, occupations, social standing, dates, rulers, cities, persecutors, and the dog’s identity because guidance does not depend on them; historians and early exegetes filled these gaps, producing divergent accounts.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#34/r1.anchor: إلى غير ذلك من الأمور التي لا يتوقف غرض الهداية على العلم بشيء منها كما يتوقف عليه غرض البحث التاريخي

TABATABAI:18:9-26#35/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#35/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#35/r1.claim: After 309 years God raised the youths to show how He had rescued them; they awoke disoriented, and some guessed they had slept a day or part of one while others deferred to God’s knowledge.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#35/r1.anchor: بعثهم بعد هذا الدهر الطويل وهو ثلاثمائة وتسع سنين من يوم دخلوا الكهف

TABATABAI:18:9-26#35/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#35/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#35/r2.claim: Because they were hungry, the youths sent one with their silver to find wholesome food and instructed him to act discreetly, fearing stoning or forced return to their religion.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#35/r2.anchor: فإنكم جياع وليتلطف الذاهب منكم إلى المدينة في مسيره إليها وشرائه الطعام ولا يشعرن بكم أحدا

TABATABAI:18:9-26#35/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#35/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#35/r3.claim: God allowed their discovery after the persecuting generation and its rule had passed; the new population, dominated by monotheists and disputing resurrection, would receive a sign of it.
