ITQAN:v1p92/r2.anchor: وقد قال محمد بن سيرين سألت عبيدة عن آية من القرآن فقال اتق الله وقل سدادا ذهب الذين يعلمون فيم أنزل الله القرآن

ITQAN:v1p92/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p92/r6.speaker: ابن تيمية
ITQAN:v1p92/r6.claim: Ibn Taymiyya distinguishes a true occasion from a case included under a verse; Bukhari treats a Companion’s bare phrase as musnad, while many others see tafsir unless the cause is explicit.
ITQAN:v1p92/r6.anchor: وقال ابن تيمية قولهم نزلت هذه الآية في كذا يراد به تارة سبب النزول ويراد به تارة أن ذلك داخل في الآية وإن لم يكن السبب

ITQAN:v1p92/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p92/r7.speaker: الزركشي
ITQAN:v1p92/r7.claim: Al-Zarkashi says Companions and Successors usually mean that a verse includes the stated ruling, not that the event caused its revelation.
ITQAN:v1p92/r7.anchor: وقال الزركشي في البرهان قد عرف من عادة الصحابة والتابعين أن أحدهم إذا قال

DAMGHANI:v1p73/r4.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p73/r4.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p73/r4.claim: Baʿth can mean sending a messenger or dispatching someone; messenger passages are grouped with this usage.
DAMGHANI:v1p73/r4.anchor: البعث يعني إرسال الرسول . قوله تعالى في سورة الجمعة

DAMGHANI:v1p18/r9.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p18/r9.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p18/r9.claim: The one sent to the city with the money is identified as Malyakhā.

DAMGHANI:v1p18/r12.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p18/r12.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p18/r12.claim: In the warning not to let anyone know about them, aḥad refers to Diqyanus.
DAMGHANI:v1p18/r12.anchor: اراد به دقيانوس قوله تعالى في سورة الكهف

DAMGHANI:v1p18/r13.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p18/r13.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p18/r13.claim: The heading also lists the king’s cupbearer as an eighth referent for aḥad, without giving its example in this excerpt.
DAMGHANI:v1p18/r13.anchor: احد من الخلق . دقيانوس . ساقي الملك

DAMGHANI:v1p218/r4.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p218/r4.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p218/r4.claim: Azka means more lawful: the sleepers ask which food is more lawful.
DAMGHANI:v1p218/r4.anchor: قوله تعالى في سورة الكهف " فلينظر أيها أزكى طعاما

DAMGHANI:v1p218/r12.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p218/r12.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p218/r12.claim: The four-sense heading for zawāl also lists falling and cessation or interruption; the excerpt ends before those senses are developed.
DAMGHANI:v1p218/r12.anchor: ز ول على أربعة أوجه كنتم كذلك السقوط الانقطاع خر فوجه منها

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p560/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p560/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p560/r1.claim: مدينة follows the pattern فعيلة and its plural is مدن.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p560/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p560/r2.speaker: قطرب
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p560/r2.claim: Qutrub derives المدينة from دان, meaning to obey.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p560/r2.anchor: قال قطرب : هي من دان ، أي أطاع

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p560/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p560/r3.speaker: ابن فارس
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p560/r3.claim: Ibn Fāris reports an etymology connecting المدينة with الدين, meaning obedience; one explanation is that obedience to the governor is established there.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p560/r3.anchor: وقال ابن فارس : قال قوم : المدينة من الدين . والدين : الطاعة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p560/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p560/r4.speaker: ابن فارس
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p560/r4.claim: Another proposed etymology connects the city with its people's dīn because they are under someone's rule or ownership.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p560/r4.anchor: وقال آخرون سميت مدينة ] لأنها دين أهلها . أي : ملكوا

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p560/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p560/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p560/r5.claim: The expressions دان بني فلان and في دين فلان show that the verb can mean ruling people and that dīn can mean obedience to someone.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p560/r5.anchor: يقال : دان فلان بني فلان ، أي : ملكهم . وفلان في دين فلان . أي : في طاعته

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p560/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p560/r6.speaker: النابغة
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p560/r6.claim: Al-Nābigha's line uses دين for people who are subject to their leader.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p560/r6.anchor: قال النابغة : بعثت على البرية خير راع … فأنت إمامها والناس دين

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p560/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p560/r7.speaker: الحطيئة
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p560/r7.claim: Al-Ḥuṭayʾa's line is cited as usage of دين for being ruled or managed.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p560/r7.anchor: وقال الحطيئة : - لقد دينت أمهر بنيك حتى … تركتهم أدق من الطحين

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p560/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p560/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p560/r8.claim: A slave woman can be called المدينة because she is owned and subdued; al-Akhṭal's ابن مدينة means the son of a slave woman.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p560/r8.anchor: ويقال للأمة : المدينة ، لأنها مملوكة مذللة ، قال الأخطل : ربت وربا في حجرها ابن مدينة … يظل على مسحاته يتركل يريد ابن أمة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p560/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p560/r13.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p560/r13.claim: The المدينة in the cave youths' story is their town; Muqātil names it Ephesus.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p560/r13.anchor: الخامس : مدينة أصحاب الكهف . قال مقاتل : واسمها أفسوس . ومنه قوله تعالى : ﴿ فابعثوا أحدكم بورقكم هذه إلى المدينة ﴾
